paragraphs.text: There is therefore now no condemnation to them that are in Christ Jesus.
paragraphs.original: Οὐδὲν ἄρα νῦν κατάκριμα τοῖς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: Ouden ara nyn katakrima tois en Christō Iēsou·

paragraphs.text: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus made me free from the law of sin and of death.
paragraphs.original: ὁ γὰρ νόμος τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς ζωῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ἠλευθέρωσέν σε ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τῆς ἁμαρτίας καὶ τοῦ θανάτου.
paragraphs.translit: ho gar nomos tou pneumatos tēs zōēs en Christō Iēsou ēleutherōsen se apo tou nomou tēs hamartias kai tou thanatou.

paragraphs.text: For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God, sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh:
paragraphs.original: τὸ γὰρ ἀδύνατον τοῦ νόμου, ἐν ᾧ ἠσθένει διὰ τῆς σαρκός, ὁ θεὸς τὸν ἑαυτοῦ υἱὸν πέμψας ἐν ὁμοιώματι σαρκὸς ἁμαρτίας καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας κατέκρινε τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἐν τῇ σαρκί,
paragraphs.translit: to gar adynaton tou nomou, en hō ēsthenei dia tēs sarkos, ho theos ton heautou hyion pempsas en homoiōmati sarkos hamartias kai peri hamartias katekrine tēn hamartian en tē sarki,

paragraphs.text: that the ordinance of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.
paragraphs.original: ἵνα τὸ δικαίωμα τοῦ νόμου πληρωθῇ ἐν ἡμῖν τοῖς μὴ κατὰ σάρκα περιπατοῦσιν ἀλλὰ κατὰ πνεῦμα·
paragraphs.translit: hina to dikaiōma tou nomou plērōthē en hēmin tois mē kata sarka peripatousin alla kata pneuma·

paragraphs.text: For they that are after the flesh mind the things of the flesh; but they that are after the Spirit the things of the Spirit.
paragraphs.original: οἱ γὰρ κατὰ σάρκα ὄντες τὰ τῆς σαρκὸς φρονοῦσιν, οἱ δὲ κατὰ πνεῦμα τὰ τοῦ πνεύματος.
paragraphs.translit: hoi gar kata sarka ontes ta tēs sarkos phronousin, hoi de kata pneuma ta tou pneumatos.

paragraphs.text: For the mind of the flesh is death; but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace:
paragraphs.original: τὸ γὰρ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς θάνατος, τὸ δὲ φρόνημα τοῦ πνεύματος ζωὴ καὶ εἰρήνη·
paragraphs.translit: to gar phronēma tēs sarkos thanatos, to de phronēma tou pneumatos zōē kai eirēnē·

paragraphs.text: because the mind of the flesh is enmity against God; for it is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can it be:
paragraphs.original: διότι τὸ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς ἔχθρα εἰς θεόν, τῷ γὰρ νόμῳ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐχ ὑποτάσσεται, οὐδὲ γὰρ δύναται·
paragraphs.translit: dioti to phronēma tēs sarkos echthra eis theon, tō gar nomō tou theou ouch hypotassetai, oude gar dynatai·

paragraphs.text: and they that are in the flesh cannot please God.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἐν σαρκὶ ὄντες θεῷ ἀρέσαι οὐ δύνανται.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de en sarki ontes theō aresai ou dynantai.

paragraphs.text: But ye are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if so be that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you. But if any man hath not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his.
paragraphs.original: Ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐκ ἐστὲ ἐν σαρκὶ ἀλλὰ ἐν πνεύματι, εἴπερ πνεῦμα θεοῦ οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν. εἰ δέ τις πνεῦμα Χριστοῦ οὐκ ἔχει, οὗτος οὐκ ἔστιν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Hymeis de ouk este en sarki alla en pneumati, eiper pneuma theou oikei en hymin. ei de tis pneuma Christou ouk echei, houtos ouk estin autou.

paragraphs.text: And if Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin; but the spirit is life because of righteousness.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς ἐν ὑμῖν, τὸ μὲν σῶμα νεκρὸν διὰ ἁμαρτίαν, τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ζωὴ διὰ δικαιοσύνην.
paragraphs.translit: ei de Christos en hymin, to men sōma nekron dia hamartian, to de pneuma zōē dia dikaiosynēn.

paragraphs.text: But if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwelleth in you, he that raised up Christ Jesus from the dead shall give life also to your mortal bodies through his Spirit that dwelleth in you.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ ἐγείραντος τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐκ νεκρῶν οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν, ὁ ἐγείρας ἐκ νεκρῶν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν ζῳοποιήσει καὶ τὰ θνητὰ σώματα ὑμῶν διὰ τὸ ἐνοικοῦν αὐτοῦ πνεῦμα ἐν ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: ei de to pneuma tou egeirantos ton Iēsoun ek nekrōn oikei en hymin, ho egeiras ek nekrōn Christon Iēsoun zōopoiēsei kai ta thnēta sōmata hymōn dia to enoikoun autou pneuma en hymin.

paragraphs.text: So then, brethren, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live after the flesh:
paragraphs.original: Ἄρα οὖν, ἀδελφοί, ὀφειλέται ἐσμέν, οὐ τῇ σαρκὶ τοῦ κατὰ σάρκα ζῆν,
paragraphs.translit: Ara oun, adelphoi, opheiletai esmen, ou tē sarki tou kata sarka zēn,

paragraphs.text: for if ye live after the flesh, ye must die; but if by the Spirit ye put to death the deeds of the body, ye shall live.
paragraphs.original: εἰ γὰρ κατὰ σάρκα ζῆτε μέλλετε ἀποθνῄσκειν, εἰ δὲ πνεύματι τὰς πράξεις τοῦ σώματος θανατοῦτε, ζήσεσθε.
paragraphs.translit: ei gar kata sarka zēte mellete apothnēskein, ei de pneumati tas praxeis tou sōmatos thanatoute, zēsesthe.

paragraphs.text: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are sons of God.
paragraphs.original: ὅσοι γὰρ πνεύματι θεοῦ ἄγονται, οὗτοι υἱοί εἰσιν θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hosoi gar pneumati theou agontai, houtoi hyioi eisin theou.

paragraphs.text: For ye received not the spirit of bondage again unto fear; but ye received the spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father.
paragraphs.original: οὐ γὰρ ἐλάβετε πνεῦμα δουλείας πάλιν εἰς φόβον, ἀλλὰ ἐλάβετε πνεῦμα υἱοθεσίας ἐν ᾧ κράζομεν· Αββα ὁ πατήρ·
paragraphs.translit: ou gar elabete pneuma douleias palin eis phobon, alla elabete pneuma hyiothesias en hō krazomen· Abba ho patēr·

paragraphs.text: The Spirit himself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are children of God:
paragraphs.original: αὐτὸ τὸ πνεῦμα συμμαρτυρεῖ τῷ πνεύματι ἡμῶν ὅτι ἐσμὲν τέκνα θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: auto to pneuma symmartyrei tō pneumati hēmōn hoti esmen tekna theou.

paragraphs.text: and if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with [him], that we may be also glorified with [him].
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ τέκνα, καὶ κληρονόμοι· κληρονόμοι μὲν θεοῦ, συγκληρονόμοι δὲ Χριστοῦ, εἴπερ συμπάσχομεν ἵνα καὶ συνδοξασθῶμεν.
paragraphs.translit: ei de tekna, kai klēronomoi· klēronomoi men theou, synklēronomoi de Christou, eiper sympaschomen hina kai syndoxasthōmen.

paragraphs.text: For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed to us-ward.
paragraphs.original: Λογίζομαι γὰρ ὅτι οὐκ ἄξια τὰ παθήματα τοῦ νῦν καιροῦ πρὸς τὴν μέλλουσαν δόξαν ἀποκαλυφθῆναι εἰς ἡμᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: Logizomai gar hoti ouk axia ta pathēmata tou nyn kairou pros tēn mellousan doxan apokalyphthēnai eis hēmas.

paragraphs.text: For the earnest expectation of the creation waiteth for the revealing of the sons of God.
paragraphs.original: ἡ γὰρ ἀποκαραδοκία τῆς κτίσεως τὴν ἀποκάλυψιν τῶν υἱῶν τοῦ θεοῦ ἀπεκδέχεται·
paragraphs.translit: hē gar apokaradokia tēs ktiseōs tēn apokalypsin tōn hyiōn tou theou apekdechetai·

paragraphs.text: For the creation was subjected to vanity, not of its own will, but by reason of him who subjected it, in hope
paragraphs.original: τῇ γὰρ ματαιότητι ἡ κτίσις ὑπετάγη, οὐχ ἑκοῦσα ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸν ὑποτάξαντα, ἐφʼ ἑλπίδι
paragraphs.translit: tē gar mataiotēti hē ktisis hypetagē, ouch hekousa alla dia ton hypotaxanta, ephʼ helpidi

paragraphs.text: that the creation itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the liberty of the glory of the children of God.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι καὶ αὐτὴ ἡ κτίσις ἐλευθερωθήσεται ἀπὸ τῆς δουλείας τῆς φθορᾶς εἰς τὴν ἐλευθερίαν τῆς δόξης τῶν τέκνων τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hoti kai autē hē ktisis eleutherōthēsetai apo tēs douleias tēs phthoras eis tēn eleutherian tēs doxēs tōn teknōn tou theou.

paragraphs.text: For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now.
paragraphs.original: οἴδαμεν γὰρ ὅτι πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις συστενάζει καὶ συνωδίνει ἄχρι τοῦ νῦν·
paragraphs.translit: oidamen gar hoti pasa hē ktisis systenazei kai synōdinei achri tou nyn·

paragraphs.text: And not only so, but ourselves also, who have the first-fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for [our] adoption, [to wit], the redemption of our body.
paragraphs.original: οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ αὐτοὶ τὴν ἀπαρχὴν τοῦ πνεύματος ἔχοντες ἡμεῖς καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς στενάζομεν, υἱοθεσίαν ἀπεκδεχόμενοι τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν τοῦ σώματος ἡμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ou monon de, alla kai autoi tēn aparchēn tou pneumatos echontes hēmeis kai autoi en heautois stenazomen, hyiothesian apekdechomenoi tēn apolytrōsin tou sōmatos hēmōn.

paragraphs.text: For in hope were we saved: but hope that is seen is not hope: for who hopeth for that which he seeth?
paragraphs.original: τῇ γὰρ ἐλπίδι ἐσώθημεν· ἐλπὶς δὲ βλεπομένη οὐκ ἔστιν ἐλπίς, ὃ γὰρ βλέπει τίς ἐλπίζει;
paragraphs.translit: tē gar elpidi esōthēmen· elpis de blepomenē ouk estin elpis, ho gar blepei tis elpizei;

paragraphs.text: But if we hope for that which we see not, [then] do we with patience wait for it.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ ὃ οὐ βλέπομεν ἐλπίζομεν, διʼ ὑπομονῆς ἀπεκδεχόμεθα.
paragraphs.translit: ei de ho ou blepomen elpizomen, diʼ hypomonēs apekdechometha.

paragraphs.text: And in like manner the Spirit also helpeth our infirmity: for we know not how to pray as we ought; but the Spirit himself maketh intercession for [us] with groanings which cannot be uttered;
paragraphs.original: Ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα συναντιλαμβάνεται τῇ ἀσθενείᾳ ἡμῶν· τὸ γὰρ τί προσευξώμεθα καθὸ δεῖ οὐκ οἴδαμεν, ἀλλὰ αὐτὸ τὸ πνεῦμα ὑπερεντυγχάνει στεναγμοῖς ἀλαλήτοις,
paragraphs.translit: Hōsautōs de kai to pneuma synantilambanetai tē astheneia hēmōn· to gar ti proseuxōmetha katho dei ouk oidamen, alla auto to pneuma hyperentynchanei stenagmois alalētois,

paragraphs.text: and he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to [the will of] God.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἐραυνῶν τὰς καρδίας οἶδεν τί τὸ φρόνημα τοῦ πνεύματος, ὅτι κατὰ θεὸν ἐντυγχάνει ὑπὲρ ἁγίων.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eraunōn tas kardias oiden ti to phronēma tou pneumatos, hoti kata theon entynchanei hyper hagiōn.

paragraphs.text: And we know that to them that love God all things work together for good, [even] to them that are called according to [his] purpose.
paragraphs.original: Οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι τοῖς ἀγαπῶσι τὸν θεὸν πάντα συνεργεῖ εἰς ἀγαθόν, τοῖς κατὰ πρόθεσιν κλητοῖς οὖσιν.
paragraphs.translit: Oidamen de hoti tois agapōsi ton theon panta synergei eis agathon, tois kata prothesin klētois ousin.

paragraphs.text: For whom he foreknew, he also foreordained [to be] conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren:
paragraphs.original: ὅτι οὓς προέγνω, καὶ προώρισεν συμμόρφους τῆς εἰκόνος τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν πρωτότοκον ἐν πολλοῖς ἀδελφοῖς·
paragraphs.translit: hoti hous proegnō, kai proōrisen symmorphous tēs eikonos tou hyiou autou, eis to einai auton prōtotokon en pollois adelphois·

paragraphs.text: and whom he foreordained, them he also called: and whom he called, them he also justified: and whom he justified, them he also glorified.
paragraphs.original: οὓς δὲ προώρισεν, τούτους καὶ ἐκάλεσεν· καὶ οὓς ἐκάλεσεν, τούτους καὶ ἐδικαίωσεν· οὓς δὲ ἐδικαίωσεν, τούτους καὶ ἐδόξασεν.
paragraphs.translit: hous de proōrisen, toutous kai ekalesen· kai hous ekalesen, toutous kai edikaiōsen· hous de edikaiōsen, toutous kai edoxasen.

paragraphs.text: What then shall we say to these things? If God [is] for us, who [is] against us?
paragraphs.original: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν πρὸς ταῦτα; εἰ ὁ θεὸς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, τίς καθʼ ἡμῶν;
paragraphs.translit: Ti oun eroumen pros tauta; ei ho theos hyper hēmōn, tis kathʼ hēmōn;

paragraphs.text: He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not also with him freely give us all things?
paragraphs.original: ὅς γε τοῦ ἰδίου υἱοῦ οὐκ ἐφείσατο, ἀλλὰ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πάντων παρέδωκεν αὐτόν, πῶς οὐχὶ καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα ἡμῖν χαρίσεται;
paragraphs.translit: hos ge tou idiou hyiou ouk epheisato, alla hyper hēmōn pantōn paredōken auton, pōs ouchi kai syn autō ta panta hēmin charisetai;

paragraphs.text: Who shall lay anything to the charge of God`s elect? It is God that justifieth;
paragraphs.original: τίς ἐγκαλέσει κατὰ ἐκλεκτῶν θεοῦ; θεὸς ὁ δικαιῶν·
paragraphs.translit: tis enkalesei kata eklektōn theou; theos ho dikaiōn·

paragraphs.text: who is he that condemneth? It is Christ Jesus that died, yea rather, that was raised from the dead, who is at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us.
paragraphs.original: τίς ὁ κατακρινῶν; Χριστὸς ὁ ἀποθανών, μᾶλλον δὲ ἐγερθείς, ὅς καί ἐστιν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὃς καὶ ἐντυγχάνει ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν·
paragraphs.translit: tis ho katakrinōn; Christos ho apothanōn, mallon de egertheis, hos kai estin en dexia tou theou, hos kai entynchanei hyper hēmōn·

paragraphs.text: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or anguish, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?
paragraphs.original: τίς ἡμᾶς χωρίσει ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ Χριστοῦ; θλῖψις ἢ στενοχωρία ἢ διωγμὸς ἢ λιμὸς ἢ γυμνότης ἢ κίνδυνος ἢ μάχαιρα;
paragraphs.translit: tis hēmas chōrisei apo tēs agapēs tou Christou; thlipsis ē stenochōria ē diōgmos ē limos ē gymnotēs ē kindynos ē machaira;

paragraphs.text: Even as it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; We were accounted as sheep for the slaughter.
paragraphs.original: καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Ἕνεκεν σοῦ θανατούμεθα ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν, ἐλογίσθημεν ὡς πρόβατα σφαγῆς.
paragraphs.translit: kathōs gegraptai hoti Heneken sou thanatoumetha holēn tēn hēmeran, elogisthēmen hōs probata sphagēs.

paragraphs.text: Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλʼ ἐν τούτοις πᾶσιν ὑπερνικῶμεν διὰ τοῦ ἀγαπήσαντος ἡμᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: allʼ en toutois pasin hypernikōmen dia tou agapēsantos hēmas.

paragraphs.text: For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers,
paragraphs.original: πέπεισμαι γὰρ ὅτι οὔτε θάνατος οὔτε ζωὴ οὔτε ἄγγελοι οὔτε ἀρχαὶ οὔτε ἐνεστῶτα οὔτε μέλλοντα οὔτε δυνάμεις
paragraphs.translit: pepeismai gar hoti oute thanatos oute zōē oute angeloi oute archai oute enestōta oute mellonta oute dynameis

paragraphs.text: nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
paragraphs.original: οὔτε ὕψωμα οὔτε βάθος οὔτε τις κτίσις ἑτέρα δυνήσεται ἡμᾶς χωρίσαι ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ θεοῦ τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: oute hypsōma oute bathos oute tis ktisis hetera dynēsetai hēmas chōrisai apo tēs agapēs tou theou tēs en Christō Iēsou tō kyriō hēmōn.
